ja: אלאנתפאע בכל ואחד מנהם. ואן כאן אחדהם אקדר עלי ד'לך מן סאירהם, פקוהֵ תוכלה עליה תכון בחסב ד'לך, ואן כאן תוכלה עלי סאירהם. ואד'א כאן לא יקדר עלי נפעה וצ'רה גיר אלואחד מנהם פקט, פבאלצ'רורה אנה יתוכל עליה וחדה, אד' לא ירג'ו מנפעה מן גירה. וכד'לך אד'א שער אלאנסאן באן לא ינפעה ולא יצ'רה אחד מן אלמכ'לוקין אלא באד'ן אללה תעאלי, אנצרף קלבה מן כ'ופהם ורג'איהם ותוכל עלי אלכ'אלק ג'ל ועז וחדה, כקולה אל תבטחו בנדיבים בבן אדם שאין לו תשועה. ואלסאדס אן יעלם עט'ים נעמה עלי אלאנסאן, ומא אבתדאה בה מן ג'זיל אלפצ'ל ואלאחסאן לגיר אסתחקאק מנה לדיה, ולא לחאג'ה מנה אליה, בל ג'ודא ואחסאנא ופצ'לא ותכרמא עלי מא צרחנא פי באב אלאעתבאר מן הד'א אלכתאב, כקול אלולי ע"ס רבות עשית אתה ה' אלהי נפלאותיך ומחשבותיך אלינו אין ערוך אליך אגידה ואדברה עצמו מספר. ואלסאבע אן יצח ענדה אן לכל מכוון פי הד'א אלעאלם מן ג'והר וערץ' חדא מעלומא לא יזיד ולא ינקץ עלי מא קדרה אלכ'אלק תעאלי פי כמיתה וכיפיתה וזמאנה ומכאנה, לא מכת'ר למא קדר תקלילה, ולא מקלל למא קדר תכת'ירה, ולא מוכ'ר למא קדר תקדימה, ולא מקדם למא קדר תאכ'ירה. ומא כאן מן אלאמור עלי כ'לאף ד'לך פהו אלמקדר אלד'י סבק פי אול אלעלם, אלא אן לג'מיע אלאקדאר אלסאבקה פי עלם אללה עז וג'ל אסבאב, וללאסבאב אסבאב, פמן ג'הל אמור אלעאלם ט'ן אן אלסבב אלחאדת' אוג'ב תגייר אלאמור ותקלבהא

**The seventh** — that the one upon whom one relies be at the utmost of generosity and at the limit of bounty toward the one who deserves it and the one who does not deserve it; and that his generosity be successive and his bounty continuous, neither cut off nor severed.

In whom all of this has been gathered, together with what has been mentioned before, the conditions of reliance in him have been completed. And it is incumbent upon the one who has known this of him to rely upon him and to repose upon him in his outer and inner state, in his heart and his limbs; to surrender to him; to be content with his decree; and to have good opinion of him in all his judgments and his actions.

When we examine these seven conditions, we do not find them gathered in created beings. We find them all in the Creator (exalted be He). As for His being merciful to His creatures: as He said, "Merciful and gracious is the Lord" (Psalms 103:8); and He said, "And shall I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city?" (Jonah 4:11). As for His being not heedless: as the Friend (peace be upon him) said, "Behold, He neither slumbers nor sleeps, the Keeper of Israel" (Psalms 121:4). As for His being not ignorant and not overcome: as He said, "Wise of heart and mighty in strength — who has hardened himself against Him and remained whole?" (Job 9:4); and He said, "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness, and the power, and the splendor, and the victory, and the majesty" (1 Chronicles 29:11); and He said, "The Lord your God is in your midst, a mighty One who saves" (Zephaniah 3:17). As for His being unique in the management of the human from the beginning of his affair and the start of his being: as Scripture said, "Is He not your father who has acquired you? He has made you and established you" (Deuteronomy 32:6); and He said, "Upon You I was sustained from the womb; from my mother's belly You are my support" (Psalms 71:6); and He said, "Did You not pour me out as milk and curdle me like cheese?" (Job 10:10), and the rest of the passage. As for His benefit and harm being subject to no one's authority but the Creator's (exalted be He): as Scripture said, "Who can speak and have it come to be, if the Lord has not commanded? From the mouth of the Most High does not the bad and the good go forth?" (Lamentations 3:37–38); and He said, "The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God shall stand forever" (Isaiah 40:8); and He said, "Surely the people are grass" (Isaiah 40:7) — and this concept has been validly established in the Third Treatise of this book sufficiently. As for His generosity being general and His bounty extending to all: as He said, "Good is the Lord to all, and His mercy is upon all His works" (Psalms 145:9); and He said, "Who gives bread to all flesh, for His mercy endures forever" (Psalms 136:25); and He said, "You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor" (Psalms 145:16). The intellect itself decides that these seven concepts are gathered in the Creator (exalted be He) to the exclusion of created beings; but I have brought in these *pesuqim* from the Book by way of recollection only.
